findings.title: Non-positive flusher process count can silently disable flushing
findings.body: The new --flusher-processes option accepts any integer. A value of 0 is silently treated as unspecified because of `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, while a negative value makes num_processes negative and produces an empty process_to_shards_map. With no workers, submit() has no buffers or backpressure state to check but still forwards messages to the committer, so spans can be committed and accumulate in Redis without ever being flushed. Fail fast on flusher_processes < 1 (and on an empty assigned-shard set) instead of starting a consumer with no flusher.

findings.title: join() can leave most flusher processes running after the timeout expires
findings.body: join() computes the deadline before calling self.next_step.join(timeout), which may consume the entire timeout, and then breaks out of the process loop when no time remains. terminate() is only reached for processes the loop has already visited, so remaining spawn processes are neither terminated nor joined. Because strategies are closed/joined and recreated in the same parent process during rebalancing, leftover daemon flushers can keep polling their shards alongside the replacement SpanFlusher and race it to produce segments. All processes should be signalled to stop/terminate before waiting on each of them subject to the deadline.

findings.title: Unhealthy flusher is replaced before the old worker has actually stopped
findings.body: _ensure_processes_alive() only signals a spawn process with kill() and never waits for it to exit; for threading.Thread workers the isinstance check skips termination entirely. It then immediately starts a replacement and overwrites self.processes/self.buffers for the same shards, losing the handle to the old worker. The old and new workers can therefore both run SpanFlusher.main() over the same shards, concurrently calling flush_segments/produce/done_flush_segments and potentially producing duplicate segments. The old worker should be terminated and joined (and the thread-based test path handled explicitly) before its replacement is started.

findings.title: Comma-joined shard list corrupts flusher metric tags
findings.body: When one worker handles multiple shards (including the CLI default of one flusher process), shard_tag is a value such as '0,1,2'. Passing that as a single statsd-style tag value means the commas are interpreted as tag separators, yielding shard=0 plus stray tags '1' and '2' and losing correct per-shard attribution; the wait_produce timer also inconsistently uses the key 'shards' instead of 'shard'. Emit metrics per shard or use a sanitized, single-valued tag consistently.

findings.title: Multiprocess flusher test checks counts but not shard routing or delivery
findings.body: test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts that there are two processes and that the shard lists total four entries. A broken mapping with duplicated and missing shards (for example [[0, 0], [1, 2]]) would still pass, and the test never submits spans or asserts that segments from each assigned shard are produced. The core new behavior (exact shard assignment, multi-worker flushing, and aggregation across workers) is therefore untested; add an end-to-end multi-partition case asserting the exact shard set and the produced segment payloads.
